  You are revising ADR-0012 at D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d/docs/architecture/adr-0012-graph-propagation-scheme.md (project D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d, Godot 4.7.2 GDScript) after per-ADR engine and TD-ADR reviews and a cross-ADR adjudication of the Core tier. Autonomous mode: "Revise flagged items". Apply every BLOCKING finding and every ruling you own; align your references to rulings owned by other ADRs without taking over their decisions; apply non-blocking findings unless clearly wrong (decline with a reason). Do not apply rejected findings. Edit only this file (grep and bounded reads; whole-file reads over 40 KB are refused). Keep Status Proposed. Replace the pending Review Log line with a Review Log dated 2026-10-29 listing each finding/ruling id and what was done. Never run git; do not edit registries, GDDs or other ADRs.
  
  ADR-0012 review verdict CONCERNS (engine seat, Godot 4.7.2). One blocking finding (E1), a trivial snippet fix. The design is idiomatic for 4.7.2 and uses no deprecated or post-cutoff API.
  
  Checks that came out clean:
  - No `const` holds a constructed object. Only int constants appear (`RNG_*`, `HOOK_*`).
  - The 4.7 typed-return override rule does not apply: the hooks are bound `Callable`s, not overrides.
  - The 4.7 rule that packed-array element writes skip setters is harmless, because the Graph declares no setters.
    - Probe on 4.7.2: `h.col[1] = 9` ran 0 setter calls; whole-array assignment ran 1.
  - Packed-array aliasing behaves as ADR-0011 § 6.2 states.
    - A local alias sees member element writes.
    - `duplicate()` isolates a snapshot from later member writes.
    - `resize` on the member also resizes the alias, because they share one ref.
    - Reassigning the member orphans the alias.
  - No Object-method name clash. Method names such as `set_section_dormant`, `set_valve`, `draw_air`, `enter` and `run` do not clash with Object, and no member is named get, set, free or call.
  - No project class name collides with a built-in class. GraphNode and GraphEdit exist as built-ins, but `GraphNode` only appears in ADR-0011's rejected Alternative 1.
  - `Dictionary` lookup treats `StringName` and `String` keys as equal, so the `after` edge dictionaries (`{&"id": ..., &"tolerates_stale": ...}`) are fine.
  - Int64 wraps silently on overflow. The ADR relies on its D.13 bounds, which is acceptable.
  
  The "probed" claims are credible and were reproduced.
  - I re-ran `0012/probe.gd` on the mono 4.7.2 editor binary.
    - Counters: 129,452,998,661 and 129,453,260,805, matching the ADR.
    - Burst test: posmod 677.
    - Insertion sort: 3.9, 33.6 and 42.2 µs at 16, 56 and 64 entries.
    - Loops over 4,096 elements: direct 48.2 µs, indirect 77.5 µs, accumulate 136.7 µs, swap 74.9 µs.
    - clampi adds about 19 µs per 4,096 calls.
  - I hand-checked the (a) and (b) arithmetic and it holds.
  - Caveats are in E3 and E5. The loop probes use function-local arrays, and the sort probe used `while` where the ADR mandates `for` with `break`.
  - Release-export behaviour, the S1 accessor cost and S3 remain UNVERIFIED, as the ADR itself says.:
  E1 [high, BLOCKING] The Key Interfaces snippets do not load under the ADR-0010 promoted-warning gate, although the ADR says they 'follow ADR-0010 typing'. I probed them on 4.7.2 in a scratch project with INFERRED_DECLARATION, UNUSED_PARAMETER, UNTYPED_DECLARATION and the shadowing warnings at 2, as ADR-0010 § 5.1 sets them. Three failures: (1) `for k in c.exchange_link_count:` in PhaseExchange.run fails with 'for iterator variable k has an implicitly inferred static type (Warning treated as error)'. ADR-0010 § 3 line 142 requires typed iterators (`for i: int in n`). The same applies to the `for j in range(...)` of the § 5 insertion sort. (2) `hook_power(views: SimViews, scope, ctx)` never uses `views`, so UNUSED_PARAMETER is an error ('The parameter views is never used ... prefix it with an underscore'). All three hook skeletons need `_views`. (3) The PhaseExchange.run excerpt leaves `d` and `scope` unused, which is the same error unless the real body uses them. Everything else in the snippets (GraphRules, IntMath calls, `const RNG_*`, `## @hot` doc comments, static-only classes) loaded clean with no shadowing hits.
    amendment: In § Key Interfaces and § 1 change `for k in c.exchange_link_count:` to `for k: int in c.exchange_link_count:`, and write the § 5 sort as `for j: int in range(i - 1, -1, -1)`. Rename the unused parameter to `_views` in `hook_power`, `hook_atmo` and `hook_failure`. Either use `d` and `scope` in the PhaseExchange excerpt or prefix them with an underscore. Add the sentence 'load-checked in a scratch project 2026-10-29 under the ADR-0010 warning set' only after re-probing.
  E2 [medium] `run_failure(..., rng: RngFacet, w)` cannot implement § 8.2. ADR-0005 defines `RngFacet.draw(stream: RngStream, counter: int)`, and the `RngStream` handle `_stream_fail` lives in GraphModule (the registration comment). No parameter of `run_failure` carries it, and `burst_hit(rng.draw(stream, ...))` in § 8.2 names a `stream` that is not in scope. Passing the facet alone is not enough.
    amendment: Change the signature to `run_failure(s, c, x, d, t, step_no, scope, rng: RngFacet, stream: RngStream, w)`, with `hook_failure` passing `_stream_fail`. Alternatively inject a small `GraphDraw` object holding both. State which in Key Interfaces.
  E3 [medium] The PhaseExchange excerpt contradicts the ADR's own § 2 rule (alias a column in a local for the phase) and the probe basis for the quoted costs. Probes (d), (e) and (f) measure function-local PackedArrays. The excerpt reads six columns through object members (`c.comp_v`, `c.edge_a_comp_row`, `c.edge_b_comp_row`, `c.edge_area_m`, `c.exchange_link_count`) and calls `s._c_n_total_at()` twice per link. My probe on the 4.7.2 editor binary, per 4,096-element read-modify-write: object member `h.col[i] = h.col[i] + 1` 262 µs (64 ns per element), local alias 55 µs (13 ns), a one-line method accessor about 117 ns per call, and a static `floor_div`-like call about 123 ns. So the '5 ns per element' and '4 ns per call' figures hold only for locals and cannot be extrapolated to member access (about 5x). The phase budget rests on D.16 coefficients and S1, which is fine, but the excerpt models the slow pattern. `_c_n_total_at` is a private-by-convention method of GraphState that is declared in no ADR (ADR-0011 does not list it). It compiles, but another class calls it across the writer-file boundary.
    amendment: In the excerpt take locals before the loop (`var n_o2: PackedInt64Array = s.n_o2`, `var n_inert: PackedInt64Array = s.n_inert`, `var va: PackedInt32Array = c.comp_v`, and so on) and compute `n_o2[ra] + n_inert[ra]` inline instead of `s._c_n_total_at(...)`. Add one sentence to § 13.1 and Performance Implications: 'probes (d) to (f) are local-array costs; member access measured about 64 ns per element and a method or static call about 120 ns on the editor binary; S1 decides'. If a helper is kept, give it a public name and list it in ADR-0011's GraphState interface.
  E4 [medium] The `pending_draw` sort key `(cid << 24) | (crew << 8) | arrival_index` gives arrival_index 8 bits, but the queue bound in § 5 and ADR-0011 § 3.8 is `MAX_CREW x compartment count`. That is 4 x 14 = 56 at MVP but 4 x about 120 = 480 in VS-A, more if a caller enqueues once per tick (6 per step). An arrival_index of 256 or more carries into the crew field. GDScript int64 never faults, so the (compartment, crew) order claimed in § 5 is silently corrupted, and the grant between two crew in a thin room becomes order-dependent. The trace key `(subject_ref << 16) | (kind << 8) | arrival_index` is safe at the 16-entry bound.
    amendment: Widen the draw key to `(cid << 32) | (crew << 16) | arrival_index` (all three fields are far below 2^31 and 2^16), or keep the layout and add a `GRAPH_BOOT_TUNING` check that the bound is at most 255. State the bit widths in the § 5 text and in the HOT-01 and unit-test fixtures.
  E5 [low] Probe (c) timed a `while` insertion sort, but PROP-01 (Foundation Ask 3) bans `while` in propagate/ and § 3 mandates 'a bounded `for` with `break`'. The probed form is therefore not the shipped form. I re-timed the `for j: ... in range(i-1,-1,-1)` + `break` form on random keys: 3.5, 27.0 and 33.3 µs at 16, 56 and 64 entries (not slower than the `while` form). On reverse-sorted input at 64 entries it is 55.3 µs. The text 'at most 43 microseconds at the 64-entry bound' (Performance Implications) is a random-input figure, not a bound. The probe's 64 is also well below the VS-A queue bound (see E4).
    amendment: Replace probe (c) with the `for`+`break` form and quote the reverse-sorted worst case (about 55 µs on the editor binary) as the bound. Keep the random-input figure as typical.
  E6 [low] § 1 says 'the kernel never drops a tick at LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS 0, and a longer stall delays ticks without skipping them'. ADR-0001's forgiveness rule does drop whole lag ticks of wall time after the per-frame cap (`dropped = lag_ticks, acc <- acc mod TICK_UNITS`). What is true, and what the Graph relies on, is that the tick counter T stays gapless, so `T mod 6` hooks always run on consecutive ticks and a step is never skipped. The sentence as written is ambiguous.
    amendment: Reword to: 'the kernel may forgive lag (drop accumulated wall time, ADR-0001), but T is gapless, so no hook due on T is skipped and a step is never skipped or repeated; a cursor gap arises only from a refused or faulted hook or a restore.'
  
  ADR-0012 review verdict CONCERNS:
  T1 [high, BLOCKING] Two mutator scope rows in § 6 contradict their real callers. M19 set_section_dormant is listed as APPLY only, and the Cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0026 says "Web Map calls M19 in a P2 apply". But web-map-and-transit.md WM-7 step (6) calls M19 inside init_world under the shared INIT scope to make A, B and the pod dormant, and ADR-0011's own assumption list puts M19 in INIT. M14 set_load_request is listed as APPLY, HOOK. But ADR-0017 (D3.4 E1, line 565, and its ask at line 978) calls M14 from the INIT-scope E1 and assumes "the INIT-scope deposit drains at the first power hook". The § 5 drain rule has no definition for an INIT deposit. As written, the new-game build would get REFUSED from M19, which fails the build with SL_NEW_GAME_NO_BASELINE, and armed lamps would have no defined drain tick.
    amendment: In the § 6 table, set M19's scope phases to APPLY, INIT and M14's to APPLY, HOOK, INIT. Add a row to the § 5 drain table: an INIT deposit drains at phase 0 of the first graph.propagate.power execution after LOADING to RUNNING, which is the first RUNNING tick T with T mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS == hook_offset_power, and that tick matches ADR-0017 D5.2's arm_tick. State that M19 in INIT stamps dormant_since with the INIT step_no (0 for a new game), and that its TOPO/SECTION marks are discarded under ADR-0003 § 4's INIT rule (one ALL batch). Change the ADR-0026 cross-ADR assumption to "M19 in init_world under INIT and in P2 applies (departure, pod_settle, berth, reconcile), never from a Graph hook".
  T2 [high, BLOCKING] The § 11 restore-equivalence table (row 'P, p_o2, o2_pm, trend') calls the intensive caches "pure function of n, V and the persisted p_prev: DERIVED, exact". That contradicts § 2's own note: phase 0 debits n_o2 (the draw drain) and changes t (CHILL/BURN traces through add_heat), while phase 7 recomputes the caches. In the uninterrupted run, P/p_o2/o2_pm/trend therefore hold the values from the previous phase 7 between 6n+0 and 6n+2. A restore landing at 6n+0 or 6n+1 recomputes them in post_restore from the post-draw state and gets different values. Sim-side readers in that window exist: emitter.place every tick, the Interaction and Horror hooks, and Sanity's Perception filter wrapping true_value P, P_O2 and T. This table is the contract the post_restore and RE stories will be built from, so the misclassification would put a restore divergence into the design.
    amendment: Choose one and state it in § 2 and § 11. (a) Preferred: at the end of phase 0, recompute the intensive caches (P, p_o2, o2_pm, trend) for every compartment that phase 0 touched (draws and CHILL/BURN). Cost is O(touched), OWN, with no new persisted state. The caches are then a pure function of current persisted state at every tick boundary and the 'exact' label is true. Delete the 'can lag the breath by up to two ticks' note. (b) Otherwise, reclassify the row as a re-derived cache with a window of up to hook_offset_atmo ticks, name its sim readers, and add the case to RE-2's expected-divergence list. Either way, add a restore at 6n+1 after a draw and a BURN to the RE-1/RE-2 fixture set.
  T3 [medium] RE-1 is weaker than the design allows. Every hook product is persisted and the restore is byte-identical, so the graph.state hash should equal the uninterrupted run's at every tick from the restore tick t onward. The ADR only requires equality "from the first failure hook after t onward". That leaves up to five ticks unchecked and would hide a divergence that heals itself, which is the hardest kind to find later.
    amendment: In § 11 Tests and in Validation Criteria, require RE-1 equality of the graph.state hash at every tick from t+1 (the first tick executed after the restore). Keep the weaker form only as the documented fallback for the case where ADR-0011 declines the hook-product columns.
  T4 [medium] The spike gating is stated honestly: S1 gates every § 13 budget, and the ladder ends with 'the number moves, not the design'. However, Performance Implications already projects about 0.6 ms per hook at the weld set against the 0.5 ms share, and that figure divides the step evenly by three. The phase-to-hook split is fixed by the GDD (TR-lsg-009). The failure hook (damage over every active node and edge, state evaluation, a possible ensure_derived, and the descriptor build) is plausibly the heaviest, so an even-split estimate understates the worst hook. The spike share is defined per hook tick, so S1 must measure the worst single hook.
    amendment: In § 13.1, require S1/S0-f to report P99 and max per hook id (power, atmo, failure) separately, plus the failure hook on a tick where phase 9 triggers ensure_derived. The pass/fail figure against GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS is the maximum over the three hooks, not the step total divided by 3. Correct the Performance Implications sentence to say the even split is an assumption that S1 replaces. Keep Open Question 9 (P3 apportionment) with the technical-director, to be decided on S1's per-hook table.
  T5 [low] The § 5 caller table claims the Interaction, Emitter State, Horror, Controller, Assembly and Web Map hooks are all ordered after the failure hook. Those orderings belong to sibling ADRs. ADR-0019 says controller.step runs after layout.doors and before body.integrate, and says nothing about the Graph hooks. The general drain rule (the first power hook after the deposit in kernel order) is correct whatever the order turns out to be, but the table asserts facts this ADR does not control.
    amendment: Replace the named-hook row with 'any hook placed after graph.propagate.power in the compiled order: the next power-hook tick'. Keep only the edges declared by ADR-0012 or confirmed by an owner (suit.vitals after atmo, attention after power, emitter.place after failure). Name Risk 7's golden compiled-order test as the thing that pins the rest.
  T6 [low] The pending_draw sort key (cid << 24) | (crew << 8) | arrival_index gives the arrival index 8 bits. The queue bound is MAX_CREW x compartment count: 56 at MVP, but about 480 at VS-A's roughly 120 compartments. Past 255 entries the arrival field carries into the crew field. The order stays deterministic, but the stated (compartment, crew) order is violated. pending_trace's (subject_ref << 16) | (kind << 8) | arrival_index has the same 8-bit field.
    amendment: Either add to GRAPH_BOOT_TUNING an assertion that each queue bound is at most 256, or widen the arrival field to 16 bits (for example (cid << 32) | (crew << 16) | arrival_index) and show the D.13 bound for the packed key.
  T7 [low] The RNG id field is 18 bits and is asserted only at boot against MAX_GRAPH_NODES and MAX_GRAPH_EDGES. That is safe only while ids equal slot counts, i.e. under the MVP no-compaction rule. ADR-0011 sets GraphLimits.ID_MAX = 2^24 precisely because of VS-A id churn. Once compaction or churn lets ids exceed 2^18, node and edge draw keys would overlap again, which is the very defect § 8.2 fixes.
    amendment: Do one of two things. Size the id field to GraphLimits.ID_MAX: the counter becomes (step_no << 26) | (kind << 24) | id, and step_no < 2^30 keeps it under 2^56. Or state in § 8.2 that the 18-bit field is MVP-only, and add an id < 2^18 check to the CAPACITY reason of M1, can_join and the RAGGED stub path so that a later change cannot exceed it silently.
  T8 [low] § 6's Budgets bullet and § 13.6 count 'one mark_dirty per applied M13' against the Interaction hook budget (TR-interact-038). But M13 is APPLY only, and the 10 SYSTEM door resubmits per tick are P2 commands (ADR-0013/ADR-0020). The Graph's M13 cost therefore lands in P2 apply, not in the Interaction hook.
    amendment: State that check_set_opening_area and check_set_valve may run in the Interaction hook's reads or validates, while applied M13 writes run in P2 apply. S1 reports the Graph's P2 share under the TR-interact-038 load separately from the hook share.
  T9 [low] § 4 says ensure_derived builds 'the sizes of the scratch and the descriptor store', and phase 9 calls ensure_derived inside the failure hook. § 3 and § 13.2 say scratch and caches are sized only by structural mutators and post_restore, 'never in a phase'. A reader could take this to mean a resize on the hook path, which would violate HOT-01 and CNT-01.
    amendment: Reword § 4: ensure_derived recomputes counts and contents into members already sized by size_derived()/size_scratch(), and calls neither. Phase-driven connectivity changes never change row counts, so the phase-9 call cannot resize. Add the absence of resize to the phase-9 path's HOT-01 coverage.
  T10 [low] The traceability sentence is off. It says 28 rows carry ADR-0012, then '18 decided here, 11 partial, 13 owned elsewhere'. 18 + 11 = 29 because TR-lsg-020 is volunteered and not planned for ADR-0012. All 28 planned rows (requirements-traceability.md) are covered, so traceability itself is complete; only the count statement is wrong.
    amendment: Reword: '28 planned rows, all addressed (18 full, 10 partial); TR-lsg-020 is a residual this ADR adds as partial; 13 further rows are owned elsewhere and supplied here.'
  T11 [low] Right-sizing advisory. At about 150 KB the ADR carries story-level detail (the scratch inventory, the column-diff harness, per-fixture lists and the full Validation list). That suits the Graph, the simulation's core, but it raises sync cost whenever a sibling ADR or the GDD moves.
    amendment: No change is required before Accept. When the Graph epic is created, move the fixture-by-fixture Validation lists into story acceptance criteria and leave the ADR citing them by name.
  
  CROSS-ADR RULINGS (binding):
  CT-01 owner ADR-0011 (align: ADR-0013, ADR-0012, ADR-0016): Merges 0011-review items 1 (first half) and 7, 0013-review items 1 and 9, and ADR-0011 T4. ADR-0013 owns the `LayoutGraphPort` definition. ADR-0011 is the implementer and currently publishes nothing for it. The Graph facade cannot be `GraphModule` or `GraphView`: GDScript has single inheritance, and `GraphView` must stay a pure, getter-only view. The implementer therefore has to be a dedicated adapter class. It cannot sit under `ports/`, because ADR-0010 ARCH-05 requires every file under `ports/` to be `@abstract`. The out-type name is the port owner's: `SectionBases` wins, and `InstantiateResult` is deleted, not aliased. M1's call chain follows ADR-0013 (Web Map -> LM1 -> port), because Layout allocates `section_id` first.
    amendment: ADR-0011, new section 9.5 'Layout port' plus a Key Interfaces snippet: `class_name GraphLayoutAdapter extends LayoutGraphPort` in `src/sim/graph/graph_layout_adapter.gd` (outside `ports/`, ARCH-05). GraphModule.setup constructs it and exposes it as `graph.layout_port()`. It holds `GraphMutators` and `GraphView`, so `GraphView` keeps its pure getter-only contract. It implements all five methods with caller-owned outs and no allocation: (1) `check_instantiate_section(views, section_id: int, template_id: String, kind: int) -> StringName`, the pure Class A check returning the LS-18 reasons plus CAPACITY and ONSET_UNKEYED, which is the same function ADR-0012 calls `check_instantiate_section`; (2) `instantiate_section(scope, section_id, template_id, kind, out: SectionBases) -> int`, which is M1; (3) `opening_into(edge_id, out: OpeningRead) -> bool`, with `door_state` derived from `area` (LS-19); (4) `seam_openings_into(seam_id, out: SeamOpenings) -> bool`, with `opening_ids` in `socket_plan.openings` order and valid after restore; (5) `section_counts_into(section_id, out: SectionCounts) -> bool`, which reads persisted columns only (Tier S) and follows CT-03. The reads are valid in APPLY, INIT, HOOK and post_restore. The two writers are valid in APPLY and INIT. Delete `views/instantiate_result.gd`. M1's out type is ADR-0013's `SectionBases {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` (in `src/sim/layout/views/`). Update section 11 and the interfaces registry candidate to match. In the section 1 row 'init_world, binding_source' and in section 4.4, write: 'M1's only caller is Layout LM1 through `LayoutGraphPort`; LM1's callers are those ADR-0013 section 9 names (Web Map `init_world` in the INIT scope at the MVP).' ADR-0012 section 6 (M1 row and Rules) gets the same wording. ADR-0016 section 3.4's Tier S list already names these reads and needs no change.
  CT-04 owner ADR-0011 (align: ADR-0012, ADR-0017, ADR-0016, ADR-0022): Merges 0011-review items 2 and 4, 0012-review item 4(1), 0016-review item 7 (delta_w_last5) and ADR-0011 T1. The request is accepted. ADR-0012 section 11 shows that a restore landing between the power hook and the atmo or failure hook cannot rebuild `served`, `draw` or the cable net load from post-phase state. That is a real G4 divergence, and Alternative 7 does not answer it. The same argument covers the five-step `power_use` window that ADR-0012 seeds flat. Attention consumes that window, and KRN-RST-05 allows no exception list, so the window is persisted too. ADR-0012 T2 option (a), which recomputes the intensive caches at the end of phase 0, keeps P, p_o2, o2_pm and trend DERIVED and exact. The `stock_cap` reconcile already agrees with ADR-0016 section 4.4.
    amendment: ADR-0011: (a) section 3.2 adds node columns `n_served` (int32, permille) and `n_draw` (int32, dJ per step), with canonical zero on every node that is not a power consumer and range specs in `GraphSchema`. (b) Section 3.4 defines `e0` of a CABLE edge as its net load in W, with a stated sign convention and min/max. (c) Section 3.8 hdr adds `power_use_w5` (five int ints, the ADR-0012 `delta_w_last5` window). (d) The section 6.1 PERSISTED row adds 'hook products: n_served, n_draw, CABLE e0 (written by ADR-0012 phase 2 only), power_use_w5'. `served_pm` moves out of DERIVED: it is read from `n_served`. (e) Section 7.4 (3) reads: 'post_restore re-derives P, p_o2, o2_pm and trend, and never served or draw.' (f) Rewrite Alternative 7 so it rejects persisting only the intensive atmosphere values, and cite ADR-0012 section 11 for the hook products. (g) Update section 3.11, Risks 1, the performance_budgets candidate and the Validation size line to about 30.5 KB (plus 40 bytes) with about 4.6 percent headroom. (h) Remove `served_pm` from the `derived_members.json` description. (i) Add GDD sync items for LS-21, LS-4 and the TR-lsg-004 wording. (j) Close Open Question 2: the phase-0 stock reconcile is agreed with ADR-0016 section 4.4. ADR-0012 section 11 and ADR-0017 D14.4 delete their 'if ADR-0011 declines' fallback text. ADR-0012 section 11 deletes the 'power_use window seeded flat' accepted divergence and restores the window from `power_use_w5`.
  CT-05 owner ADR-0011 (align: ADR-0012, ADR-0017, ADR-0016): Merges 0011-review item 5, 0012-review item 4(2) and ADR-0011 T2. ADR-0012 section 1 owns the hook cursors and defines `last_step_no` as the last step whose failure hook completed (LS-8). ADR-0017's FAULT_GLOW reconcile and FT-15 depend on that meaning. ADR-0011 adopts it.
    amendment: ADR-0011 section 2.3, last sentence: '`hdr.last_step_no` is the last step whose failure hook (phase 11) completed (LS-8, ADR-0012 section 1). It trails `step_no()` by up to one step, and equals it only from the end of the failure hook until the next power-hook tick.' Section 3.8's hdr list and the `GraphView.last_step_no()` doc comment say the same.
  CT-06 owner ADR-0011 (align: ADR-0012): Merges 0011-review item 10, 0012-review item 2 and the GraphScratch half of 0012-review item 4(4). ADR-0012 section 3 replaces the Jacobi `next` columns with int64 delta accumulators. Probes show that swapping columns strands aliases. Of the two options for the total-amount accessor, the choice is to drop the need for it: ADR-0012 inlines `n_o2 + n_inert` and does not call `_c_n_total_at`. No new GraphState accessor is added.
    amendment: ADR-0011 section 1 table, the section 6.1 SCRATCH row and section 6.2 (4) read: '`GraphScratch` holds the ADR-0012 section 3 inventory (PackedInt64Array accumulators and the island, candidate, sort and traversal buffers), and is all zero at every hook exit. The swap-by-reference rule remains available for a future field that is rewritten wholesale.' List the accumulator members by name, and add the GraphCaches and GraphDiag members ADR-0012 introduces, plus their `derived_members.json` entries. ADR-0012 section 3 and its E3 excerpt replace `_c_n_total_at` with an inline `n_o2[s] + n_inert[s]`.
  CT-07 owner ADR-0011 (align: ADR-0012, ADR-0010): Merges 0011-review item 6, the writer-set half of 0012-review item 2, and ADR-0011 T3. ADR-0012's design writes GraphCaches from phases 7 and 11 and from every marker, including mutators, and sizes GraphScratch from the derived file. The proposed OWN-01 configuration would flag that code. The choice is option (i), explicit per-member writer files, rather than routing every write through GraphDerived: the last-emitted bucket update happens on every mark in hot code, and an extra call per mark is the wrong place to spend budget.

attachment.content:
- adopt: Brownfield audit — do existing artifacts actually work? Numbered migration plan. Unlike /project-stage-detect, checks compliance not existence.
- agents-sdk: Build, debug, or review Cloudflare Agents SDK applications using the agents package.
- architecture-decision: Create an ADR documenting a technical decision: context, alternatives considered, consequences.
- architecture-review: Traceability matrix mapping GDD requirements to ADRs. Finds gaps, cross-ADR conflicts, engine compatibility. PASS/CONCERNS/NOT ASSESSED/FAIL.
- art-bible: Author the Art Bible — visual identity gating asset production. Run before /map-systems.
- asset-audit: Audit assets against naming conventions, file size budgets, format standards. Finds orphaned assets, missing references.
- asset-spec: Per-asset visual specs plus AI generation prompts from GDDs and character profiles. After the art bible.
- balance-check: Find balance outliers, broken progressions, degenerate strategies, economy imbalances in formulas and data. 'Check game balance'.
- basin: Build and troubleshoot Cloudflare Basin analytics workflows with Basin Pipelines, Basin Catalog, and Basin SQL. Use for streaming data into R2 Iceberg tables, managing catalogs, or querying those tables; also use for requests using the former Data Platform, Pipelines, R2 Data Catalog, or R2 SQL names.
- brainstorm: Guided concept ideation using professional studio techniques, player psychology, creative exploration.
- brownfield: First-principles audit and improvement plan for an EXISTING codebase ("brownfield" project) — especially one the user can run and demo but can't confidently judge. Orchestrates parallel specialist subagents (architecture, product-intent, code, tests, security, performance, docs) that treat existing code as evidence rather than ground truth, keeps an assumptions register and escalates the risky ones, writes a consolidated improvement design doc with a dependency-ordered PR plan sized to the repo, runs a writer↔reviewer loop until no critical/major issues remain, and optionally (--execute) implements the plan as worktree-isolated, reviewed git branches. Use this skill whenever the user says /brownfield, asks to audit / health-check / assess / sanity-check / "second opinion" an existing repo or legacy app, asks "is this built correctly?", "what's wrong with this codebase?", "a contractor/AI built this and I'm not sure it's right", wants a prioritized improvement or remediation plan for code that already exists, or is inheriting a project and wants to know where the bodies are buried — even if they never use the word "brownfield". Not for greenfield design of new systems or for reviewing a single small diff/PR.
- bug-report: Structured bug report from a description, or analyze code for potential bugs. Reproduction steps, severity.
- bug-triage: Re-evaluate open bugs — priority vs severity, assign to sprints, surface systemic trends. Run when the count grows.
- ccgs-code-review: Architectural code review — coding standards, SOLID, testability, performance concerns.
- changelog: Auto-generate a changelog from git commits and sprint data. Internal and player-facing versions.
- cloudflare: Discover and choose Cloudflare products for apps, APIs, AI agents, storage, networking, and security. Use for architecture and product selection, including when the user describes a need without naming a Cloudflare product; then find the relevant skill or documentation.
- cloudflare-email-service: Implement or troubleshoot Cloudflare Email Sending and Email Routing integrations and their delivery configuration.

- k2: Build and troubleshoot Cloudflare K2 or K2 Streams durable logs. Use for stream setup, producing from Workers or HTTP, configuring retention and inputs, and consuming through subscriptions.
- launch-checklist: Launch readiness across every department: code, content, store, marketing, community, infrastructure, legal, go/no-go sign-offs.
- legion: Route legion <command> requests to the Legion CLI for Claude Code.
- localize: Localization pipeline — find hardcoded strings, extract string tables, cultural review, VO, RTL, enforce string freeze.
- map-systems: Decompose a concept into individual systems, map dependencies, prioritize design order, create the systems index.
- milestone-review: Milestone progress review — completeness, quality metrics, risk, go/no-go recommendation. At checkpoints or before a deadline.
- nextjs-on-cloudflare: Build, migrate, and deploy Next.js apps on Cloudflare Workers with vinext. Use when starting a Next.js project on Cloudflare, moving an existing app to Workers, choosing between vinext and OpenNext, or setting up vinext for Workers. For setup, migration, or deployment, install vinext's upstream skills with `npx skills add cloudflare/vinext` if missing, then read and follow the applicable skill and docs.

- orchestrate-omp: Coordinate OMP subagents on substantial work. Use when parallel discovery, specialist review, or clearly partitioned implementation will shorten or strengthen the result; skip trivial tasks.
- patch-notes: Player-facing patch notes from git history and changelogs. Translates developer language into player communication.
- perf-profile: Performance profiling — find bottlenecks, measure against budgets, produce ranked optimization recommendations.
- playtest-report: Structured playtest report template, or turn existing playtest notes into structured feedback.
- project-stage-detect: Analyze project state, detect stage, identify gaps, recommend next steps. 'Where are we in development?'
- propagate-design-change: A GDD changed — scan ADRs and the traceability index for now-stale architectural decisions. Impact report, guides resolution.
- prototype: Concept prototype before GDDs — throwaway HTML, Engine or Paper build, PROCEED/PIVOT/KILL/NOT ASSESSED. After /brainstorm and /setup-engine.
- pstack-omp: OMP adapter for poteto-mode. Maps canonical pstack roles and lifecycle protocols to current OMP task agents, batching, isolation, IRC follow-ups, and durable result resources.

# Global instructions (all projects)

## Dynamic Workflows: model choice

- Always use Sonnet 5.5 (`model: 'sonnet'`) or Haiku (`model: 'haiku'`) for worker agents in Dynamic Workflows (the Workflow tool's `agent()` calls), to preserve token usage. Use Haiku for mechanical stages (logging, formatting, simple extraction) and Sonnet for the rest.
- Opus or Fable is acceptable only as an advisor where needed: a senior reviewer, judge or verdict seat, never for bulk work such as planners, writers, fixers or scanners.
- Set `model` explicitly on every worker `agent()` call; do not let workers inherit the session model.

# Claude Code Game Studios -- Game Studio Agent Architecture

Indie game development managed through 49 coordinated Claude Code subagents.
Each agent owns a specific domain, enforcing separation of concerns and quality.

## Technology Stack

- **Engine**: Godot 4.7.2
- **Language**: GDScript
- **Version Control**: Git with trunk-based development
- **Build System**: SCons (engine), Godot Export Templates
- **Asset Pipeline**: Godot Import System + custom resource pipeline

> **Note**: Engine-specialist agents exist for Godot, Unity, and Unreal with
> dedicated sub-specialists. Use the set matching your engine.

## Project Structure

@.claude/docs/directory-structure.md

## Engine Version Reference

@docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md


## Technical Preferences

`project.yaml` at the repo root is the primary config store — engine, specialists,
naming, platform, performance, modes. Skills resolve it via `resolve_config`
(see `.claude/docs/config-resolution.md`).

`.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` is the **legacy fallback**, read on demand
when a key is absent from `project.yaml`. It is not imported here: before
`/setup-engine` runs it is almost entirely `[TO BE CONFIGURED]` placeholders, and
after it runs `project.yaml` holds the real values.

## Coordination Rules

@.claude/docs/coordination-rules.md

## Collaboration Protocol

**User-driven collaboration, not autonomous execution.**
Every task follows: **Question -> Options -> Decision -> Draft -> Approval**

- Agents MUST ask "May I write this to [filepath]?" before using Write/Edit tools
  (exempt: `active.md` appends, agent memory, a subagent's new file at the path
  its orchestrating skill named; see `.claude/rules/agent-memory.md`)
- Agents MUST show drafts or summaries before requesting approval
- Multi-file changes require explicit approval for the full changeset
- No commits without user instruction
- A skipped or dismissed question is not an answer: act on nothing, re-ask in
  plain text and wait
- Started outside this file's folder? Warn first: hooks, deny rules and the
  ask-first mode load only when Claude Code starts here

See `docs/COLLABORATIVE-DESIGN-PRINCIPLE.md` for full protocol and examples.

> **First session?** If the project has no engine configured and no game concept,
> run `/start` to begin the guided onboarding flow.

## Coding Standards

@.claude/docs/coding-standards.md

## Context Management

Read `.claude/docs/context-management.md` on demand — it is a reference, not
session context. Two of its conventions are load-bearing and cited by name
elsewhere in the repo, so they are restated here rather than lost:

- **`production/session-state/active.md` is the session checkpoint.** The file is
  the memory, not the conversation. Read it first after any compaction, crash, or
  `/clear`.
- **Helpers in `.claude/scripts/` emit observations, never verdicts.** A script
  that scores or judges will eventually contradict a mode or override it cannot
  see. (Cited by `artifact-check.sh` and `adr-dep-graph.sh`.)

# Directory Structure

```text
/
├── CLAUDE.md                    # Master configuration
├── project.yaml                 # Machine-readable project config — engine, modes, stage (source of truth)
├── .claude/                     # Agent definitions, skills, hooks, rules, docs
├── <code root>/                 # Game source code — THE PATH IS ENGINE-SPECIFIC, see below
├── assets/                      # Game assets (art, audio, vfx, shaders, data)
├── design/                      # Game design documents (gdd, narrative, levels, balance)
├── docs/                        # Technical documentation (architecture, api, postmortems)
│   └── engine-reference/        # Curated engine API snapshots (version-pinned)
├── tests/                       # Game test suites (unit, integration, performance, playtest)
├── tools/                       # Build and pipeline tools (ci, build, asset-pipeline)
├── prototypes/                  # Throwaway prototypes (outside the code root)
├── production/                  # Production management (sprints, milestones, releases)
│   ├── session-state/           # Ephemeral session state (active.md — gitignored)
│   └── session-logs/            # Session audit trail (gitignored)
└── studio-tests/                # QA for the skills/agents themselves — /skill-test, /skill-improve
```

## The code root is engine-specific

**Two of the three supported engines will not build a project whose code sits in
`src/`.** This is not a style preference — it is a hard constraint of the engine's
own toolchain:

| `engine.name` | Code root | Why it cannot be `src/` |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `src/` | No constraint — Godot loads from `res://` anywhere under the project root. |
| **Unity** | `Assets/` | Unity compiles **only** `Assets/` and `Packages/`. Code outside them is invisible to the compiler. |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/` | UnrealBuildTool discovers modules under `Source/`; content lives in `Content/`. A module elsewhere is not built. |

**Resolve the code root from `engine.name` before writing any source file.** A
path shown as `src/…` alone is a Godot example: read it as *"the code root"* and
substitute the row above. `src/` is the table's Godot row, not a universal path.

**Tests follow the same rule** — the same compilers decide what they see:

| `engine.name` | Test root | Anywhere else |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/` | — |
| **Unity** | `Assets/Tests/EditMode/`, `Assets/Tests/PlayMode/` | not compiled: "0 tests, Passed" |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/Private/Tests/` | not built: "No automation tests matched" |

Read `tests/unit/[system]/` (or `integration/`) anywhere as the test root plus `[System]/`.

# Godot Engine — Version Reference

| Field | Value |

| **Engine Version** | Godot 4.7 |

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,
  and none required at `minimal`, where the decision log and `design/game-brief.md`
  carry the rationale instead. See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.
- Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded
- All public methods must be unit-testable (dependency injection over singletons)
- Commits must reference the relevant design document or task ID
- **Commit messages**: Use Conventional Commits format — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`. Reference the story or task ID in the body (e.g., `Story: EPIC-001-S02`).
- **Verification-driven development**: Write tests first when adding gameplay systems.
  For UI changes, verify with screenshots. Compare expected output to actual output
  before marking work complete. Every implementation should have a way to prove it works.
- **A parse check is not a run.** Every story that changes something
  player-observable is launched and observed before it closes, and the
  observation is a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`. Procedure
  per engine: `.claude/docs/run-and-observe.md`. Not waived at
  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`

  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,

> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`

  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag

# Directory Structure

```text
/
├── CLAUDE.md                    # Master configuration
├── project.yaml                 # Machine-readable project config — engine, modes, stage (source of truth)
├── .claude/                     # Agent definitions, skills, hooks, rules, docs
├── <code root>/                 # Game source code — THE PATH IS ENGINE-SPECIFIC, see below
├── assets/                      # Game assets (art, audio, vfx, shaders, data)
├── design/                      # Game design documents (gdd, narrative, levels, balance)
├── docs/                        # Technical documentation (architecture, api, postmortems)
│   └── engine-reference/        # Curated engine API snapshots (version-pinned)
├── tests/                       # Game test suites (unit, integration, performance, playtest)
├── tools/                       # Build and pipeline tools (ci, build, asset-pipeline)
├── prototypes/                  # Throwaway prototypes (outside the code root)
├── production/                  # Production management (sprints, milestones, releases)
│   ├── session-state/           # Ephemeral session state (active.md — gitignored)
│   └── session-logs/            # Session audit trail (gitignored)
└── studio-tests/                # QA for the skills/agents themselves — /skill-test, /skill-improve
```

## The code root is engine-specific

**Two of the three supported engines will not build a project whose code sits in
`src/`.** This is not a style preference — it is a hard constraint of the engine's
own toolchain:

| `engine.name` | Code root | Why it cannot be `src/` |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `src/` | No constraint — Godot loads from `res://` anywhere under the project root. |
| **Unity** | `Assets/` | Unity compiles **only** `Assets/` and `Packages/`. Code outside them is invisible to the compiler. |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/` | UnrealBuildTool discovers modules under `Source/`; content lives in `Content/`. A module elsewhere is not built. |

**Resolve the code root from `engine.name` before writing any source file.** A
path shown as `src/…` alone is a Godot example: read it as *"the code root"* and
substitute the row above. `src/` is the table's Godot row, not a universal path.

**Tests follow the same rule** — the same compilers decide what they see:

| `engine.name` | Test root | Anywhere else |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/` | — |
| **Unity** | `Assets/Tests/EditMode/`, `Assets/Tests/PlayMode/` | not compiled: "0 tests, Passed" |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/Private/Tests/` | not built: "No automation tests matched" |

Read `tests/unit/[system]/` (or `integration/`) anywhere as the test root plus `[System]/`.

- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions

- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
