gdd_sync.old: **Topology refresh is one idempotent function** run at the head of whichever Graph hook runs first after a structural mutator (M1-M5): power (`T mod 6` = 0), atmo (2) or failure (4), not only at phase 1
gdd_sync.new: Topology refresh is one idempotent function (`ensure_derived`) run eagerly by every writer that changes topology (structural mutators M1-M6, M8, M9, M19; the end of phase 9 after a connectivity-changing transition; `post_restore`), with the head of each Graph hook a defect-only guard counted by `late_rebuilds`; `ensure_derived` never resizes; `degrees` and `deg_max` leave the phase-1 list and are recomputed at the head of phase 6

gdd_sync.old: `block_hash` dirty flag
gdd_sync.new: (row text deleted: the kernel invalidates the cached hash by the touch serial of every granted open_for, ADR-0005 section 5.2; the Graph does nothing)

gdd_sync.old: | 10 | failure | Cascade rules (LS-12) evaluated on this run's phase-9 states; effects queued to `forced_mode_next`, bounded by `MAX_SPREAD_PER_STEP` in ascending subject id
gdd_sync.new: | 10 | failure | Cross-subject cascade rules (LS-12) evaluated on this run's phase-9 states (a subject's own forced mode is written in phase 9); admitted candidates queue `forced_mode_next` up to `MAX_SPREAD_PER_STEP` in ascending subject id; unadmitted candidates are re-proposed next run, not stored. Phase 9 evaluates `T_mach` from the current persisted temperatures (D.8)

gdd_sync.old: LS-8 phase 0 row (inputs: stock reconcile, queue drain, forced_next apply)
gdd_sync.new: phase 0 additionally closes out the intensive caches (P, p_o2, o2_pm, trend) of every compartment it touched (draw_air debit, CHILL/BURN), so the caches are a pure function of persisted state at every tick boundary; the 'caches can lag the breath' wording is deleted

gdd_sync.old: the double-buffered `_cur` / `_next` snapshot of LS-1 (j) is confirmed to snapshot
gdd_sync.new: the live column is the start-of-phase snapshot until the end-of-phase accumulator apply (JAC, ADR-0012 section 3); no `_next` column swap is used for pairwise fluxes

gdd_sync.old: `subject_id < 2^20` is asserted
gdd_sync.new: the counter is `(step_no << 26) | rng_subject(kind, id)` with `rng_subject = (kind << 24) | id`, kind 0 node, 1 edge, 2 reserved for compartments, and `id < GraphLimits.ID_MAX <= 2^24` asserted at boot, so a node and an edge with the same number draw different values for any id the allocator can produce

gdd_sync.old: Randomness (thaw-burst only at MVP) is `rng_derive(world_seed, "graph.fail", (step_no<<20) | subject_id)`, a pure function of persisted state with no restore-epoch input, so a reload replays identical outcomes; subject_id < 2^20 asserted.
gdd_sync.new: Randomness (thaw-burst only at MVP) is `rng_derive(world_seed, "graph.fail", (step_no<<26) | rng_subject(kind, id))` with rng_subject = (kind<<24)|id (kind 0 node, 1 edge), a pure function of persisted state with no restore-epoch input, so a reload replays identical outcomes; id < GraphLimits.ID_MAX <= 2^24 asserted at boot.

gdd_sync.old: M19 also advances, by `step_no − dormant_since_step`, every subject's `mode_since_step` and non-zero `isolated_at_step` (GA-T, LS-14: a trail's age counts only the steps the section ran) **and** `warn_since_step` (while `has_warn`), `fail_since_step` (of every FAILED or DESTROYED subject) and `patched_at_step` (of every patched subject, `hp_cap` < `HP_FULL`), and every SeamRecord's `built_step` and `mode_since_step`
gdd_sync.new: M19 also advances, by `step_no − dormant_since_step`, every subject's `mode_since_step` and non-zero `isolated_at_step`, `warn_since_step` (while `has_warn`), `fail_since_step` (FAILED or DESTROYED), `patched_at_step` (`hp_cap` < `HP_FULL`), non-zero `thaw_until_step`, a LOAD's non-zero `energised_at_step`, each compartment's set `warn_since_o2/p/t`, and every SeamRecord's `built_step` and `mode_since_step`; `stress_until_step` is still not advanced; the descriptor store holds loaded sections only; M19 is callable under INIT (Web Map init_world step 6), where it stamps `dormant_since` with the INIT step_no

gdd_sync.old: `served_pm` is not, because phase 2 recomputes it before use
gdd_sync.new: `served_pm` (`n_served`), the power delivered to each consumer (`n_draw`), a cable's net load and the five-step `power_use` window (`power_use_w5`) are persisted hook products written by phase 2 only, so a restore on any tick reproduces the uninterrupted run; `post_restore` no longer derives them

gdd_sync.old: re-checks `S + D` > 0 on this run's phase-2 result
gdd_sync.new: re-checks, in phase 8, that an island at either end holds a live source from the persisted `out_w` of its sources and `stock` of its batteries

gdd_sync.old: `⌊duty_t × served_pm / 1000⌋` for a HEATER
gdd_sync.new: `⌊1000 × n_draw / max(1, req)⌋` for a HEATER (n_draw is the persisted power delivered in the last solve)

gdd_sync.old: and a hook that declares `before: graph.propagate.power` drains at 6k
gdd_sync.new: (sentence deleted: HookDescriptor has no `before` edge; a hook the compiled order places before the power hook on a power-hook tick drains on that tick)

gdd_sync.old: M17/M14/M15 deposits drain in phase 0 of the same tick when made by a P2 command or a hook ordered before graph.propagate.power, and at the next hook tick when made by a hook ordered after it, always in arrival order within the cap.
gdd_sync.new: M17/M14/M15 deposits drain in phase 0 of the first graph.propagate.power execution that follows the deposit in kernel order (tick, P2 before P3, compiled schedule position): the same tick when that tick is a power-hook tick and the deposit precedes the hook, otherwise the next power-hook tick; an INIT deposit drains at the first power-hook tick after LOADING to RUNNING; always in arrival order within the cap.

gdd_sync.old: `cause` is not in LS-3's common-field list though LS-14 returns it
gdd_sync.new: `cause` is persisted as the node/edge EXOGENOUS flag; it is set by an exogenous apply and cleared when the subject's dominant mode returns to 0 or its `hp` reaches `HP_OK` (the cause of the current episode)

gdd_sync.old: template ids unique; POWER acyclic; advances `next_section_id` to `max(section_id) + 1`
gdd_sync.new: template ids unique; POWER acyclic; `ONSET_UNKEYED` (a `mode_since_step` seeded without `mode_key`); advances `next_section_id` to `max(section_id) + 1`

gdd_sync.old: rung 1 hook stagger by offset 0 / 2 / 4 (the three hooks already exist, R3) — **the MVP baseline, not a fallback**
gdd_sync.new: the hook stagger by offset 0 / 2 / 4 is the MVP baseline (rung 0 of ADR-0010 section 9); the lever order is ADR-0012 section 13.1: tuning, then call-overhead removal (ADR-0010 rungs 1-2), then VS-A quiescence and GDExtension; the pass/fail figure is the worst single hook, not the step divided by three

gdd_sync.old: no loop iterates to a convergence condition, no function is recursive, and the only loops are bounded by a slot count, an edge count or a constant. (lint)
gdd_sync.new: enforced by lint PROP-01 over src/sim/graph/propagate/ (no while loop, no direct self-recursion, no loop bound assigned inside the loop)

gdd_sync.old: gating leak wear on `intensity_pm` > 0
gdd_sync.new: gating leak wear on the persisted `isolated_at_step` stamp (non-zero behind a closed valve), the form of the `intensity_pm` > 0 test that phase 8 can read and a restore reproduces

decisions.chosen: Option (a): phase 0 ends by recomputing P, p_o2, o2_pm and trend for every compartment it touched; caches stay DERIVED and exact at every tick boundary
decisions.reason: No new persisted state, O(touched) cost, makes the 'exact' label true and removes the restore divergence for sim readers; RE-1/RE-2 gain restore-at-6n+1 fixtures after a draw and a BURN.

decisions.chosen: (step_no << 26) | (kind << 24) | id, id sized to GraphLimits.ID_MAX = 2^24, key below 2^56
decisions.reason: Ids can exceed any slot count under VS-A churn, so an MVP-only 18-bit field would silently re-introduce node/edge key overlap; golden values computed by arithmetic, not re-probed.

decisions.chosen: (cid << 32) | (crew << 16) | arrival_index and (subject_ref << 32) | (kind << 16) | arrival_index; boot asserts queue bounds <= 65,535
decisions.reason: Widening is cheap and removes the carry into the crew field above 255 entries; D.13 bound below 2^56.

decisions.chosen: Add stream: RngStream beside rng: RngFacet; hook_failure passes _stream_fail
decisions.reason: Smallest signature change matching ADR-0005 RngFacet.draw(stream, counter); no extra object.

decisions.chosen: M19 APPLY, INIT; M14 APPLY, HOOK, INIT; INIT deposit drains at first power-hook tick after LOADING to RUNNING (= ADR-0017 arm_tick); M19 under INIT stamps dormant_since at INIT step_no with marks discarded
decisions.reason: Matches the real callers (WM-7 init_world, ADR-0017 E1) and gives the INIT deposit a defined drain tick.

decisions.chosen: RE-1 equality at every tick from t+1; no weaker fallback
decisions.reason: CT-04 has ADR-0011 persist all hook products (including power_use_w5) and deletes the 'if declines' text, so the fallback clause is dead.

decisions.chosen: ADR-0012 keeps the runtime HOOK_CURSOR (code 25) guard and the first-run hdr.sched rule; restore-time check is ADR-0011 section 7.2 step 13 (code 26)
decisions.reason: The Graph owns its fault table and restore steps; ADR-0016 covers it by reference.

decisions.chosen: Alias all columns in locals, inline n_o2[r] + n_inert[r], no GraphState accessor
decisions.reason: Member access measured about 5x slower than local arrays; ruling CT-06 drops the accessor.

decisions.chosen: Maximum over the three hook ids (P99 and max per hook), plus failure hook on a phase-9 ensure_derived tick; cite the ADR-0003 P3 share ledger row
decisions.reason: Phase-to-hook split is fixed by the GDD and the failure hook is plausibly heaviest; the 1.66 ms Core sum on a Graph tick needs a ledger, owned by ADR-0003.

open_questions: The corrected Key Interfaces snippets (typed iterators, underscore-prefixed unused parameters, locals in the PhaseExchange excerpt) have not been re-probed under the ADR-0010 section 5.1 promoted-warning set; the 'load-checked' sentence is withheld until LINT-SPIKE-1 or a re-probe.

The new RNG golden values (node 5 and edge 5 at step 123,456: 8,284,991,913,989 and 8,285,008,691,205) are shell arithmetic; ADR-0005 golden vectors for this counter must be regenerated from rng_counter.
The pending_draw insertion sort was measured only to 64 entries; the VS-A queue bound (about 480) needs an S1 re-measure and possibly a counting pass by cid (Risk 10).

Apportionment of the 2 ms P3 target among divisor-6 hooks stays with the technical-director on S1's per-hook table (Open Question 9); the ADR-0003 P3 share ledger is a foundation amendment owned elsewhere.
Whether ADR-0011 words 'closes out' the intensive caches in structural mutators via ensure_derived as this ADR states (section 2 note) needs confirming in ADR-0011's sibling revision.

declined.reason: Right-sizing advisory; the reviewer states no change is required before Accept. The fixture-by-fixture Validation lists move into story acceptance criteria when the Graph epic is created.

The sentence 'load-checked in a scratch project 2026-10-29 under the ADR-0010 warning set' was not added: the corrected snippets were not re-probed (the amendment says to add it only after re-probing). Key Interfaces says so explicitly.
The 'keep the weaker RE-1 form as the documented fallback if ADR-0011 declines the columns' clause was not kept: binding ruling CT-04 has ADR-0011 adopt the columns and deletes the fallback text.
The first option (separate stream parameter) was taken; no GraphDraw object introduced.

registry_candidates.name: graph_hook_products
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- state: graph_hook_products
  status: proposed  # ADR-0011 adopts the columns by ruling CT-04
  owner: life-support-graph
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0012-graph-propagation-scheme.md
  interface: "n_served (permille) and n_draw (dJ per step) per power consumer node, the net load of a CABLE edge (edge column e0) and the five-int header window power_use_w5, written only by propagate phase 2, canonical zero elsewhere; persisted so a restore on any tick equals the uninterrupted run"
  read_by: [emitter-state, suit, interaction, in-world-instruments, attention, failure-and-trail]
  added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: graph_propagation_hooks
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- contract: graph_propagation_hooks
  status: proposed
  pattern: kernel_hook_chain
  producer: life-support-graph
  consumers: [suit, attention, emitter-state, sanity]
  signal_signature: "three HookDescriptors graph.propagate.power/.atmo/.failure, divisor GRAPH_STEP_TICKS, offsets from GraphTuning (0,2,4) each <= divisor-2, after chain with tolerates_stale true on both edges; step_no = floor_div(clock.tick(), graph_step_ticks); cursors last_step_power/_atmo/_failure and last_step_no (the failure hook's step; trails step_no by up to one step); stored schedule hdr.sched compared at the first run after a load"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0012-graph-propagation-scheme.md
  not: "a fourth Graph hook; a before: edge; catching up a missed step"
  added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: graph_input_queue_drain
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- contract: graph_input_queue_drain
  status: proposed
  pattern: queued_unconditional_channel
  producer: life-support-graph
  consumers: [emitter-state, interaction, suit, horror, attention]
  signal_signature: "M14/M15/M17 enqueue into persisted bounded queues and drain only in phase 0 of the first graph.propagate.power execution that follows the deposit in kernel order (INIT, then tick, P2 before P3, compiled schedule position); an INIT deposit drains at the first power-hook tick after LOADING to RUNNING; grant returned only through the persisted draw_grant table"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0012-graph-propagation-scheme.md
  not: "synchronous apply of M14/M15/M17; a synchronous grant; a drain outside phase 0"
  added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: graph_write_disciplines
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: graph_write_disciplines
  status: proposed
  api: "Every Graph phase declares per written column JAC (read start-of-phase values, write a GraphScratch accumulator, apply in one ascending loop that re-zeroes it), ALLOC (ascending-id allocation against a running balance) or OWN (own row only); phases iterate derived active lists and alias columns in locals; accumulators all-zero at hook exit; phase 0 closes out the intensive caches it touched"
  not: "next-column copy and swap for pairwise fluxes; iterating to convergence; recursion; catch-up; iterating a table or Dictionary in a phase; a total-amount accessor on GraphState"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0012-graph-propagation-scheme.md
  added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: graph_fairness_gate_function
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: graph_fairness_gate_function
  status: proposed
  api: "graph_rules.gate_floor(hp_before, hull_or_seam, gate_open, hp_fail, breach_hp) and apply_loss(hp_before, loss, floor_hp): a floor applied at the moment of damage that limits the reduction and never raises hp; EXOGENOUS causes pass floor 0; the node/edge EXOGENOUS flag is the descriptor cause of the current episode"
  not: "a post-pass that rewrites hp; rate_pm or stress_pm read outside the damage phase"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0012-graph-propagation-scheme.md
  added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: graph_rng_subject_key
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: graph_rng_subject_key
  status: proposed
  api: "plain stream graph.fail; RngFacet.draw(stream, counter) with counter (step_no << 26) | (kind << 24) | id, kind 0 node, 1 edge, 2 reserved compartment, id < GraphLimits.ID_MAX <= 2^24; burst test posmod_i(raw & 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, 1000) < burst_p_pm; no stored counter; no restore epoch"
  not: "draw_epoch for a Graph draw; a node id and an edge id sharing one subject field; an id field narrower than GraphLimits.ID_MAX; a float or bare % in the burst test"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0012-graph-propagation-scheme.md
  added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: graph_derived_rebuild
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: graph_derived_rebuild
  status: proposed
  api: "GraphDerived.ensure_derived is idempotent and never resizes (size_derived/size_scratch/size_descriptors run only in structural mutators and post_restore); called by every writer that changes topology (structural mutators, end of phase 9 after a connectivity change, post_restore); the hook head guard is defect-only and counts late_rebuilds; degrees and deg_max are phase-6 scratch, not cached"
  not: "lazy-only topology refresh; a read that pays a rebuild; a hook reading a half-applied topology; a resize on the hook path"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0012-graph-propagation-scheme.md
  added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: graph_hooks
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- system: graph_hooks
  status: proposed
  budget_ms: 0.5
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0012-graph-propagation-scheme.md
  notes: "GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS spike share: P99 0.5 and max 1.0 on a release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; pass/fail on the maximum over the three hook ids (power, atmo, failure) reported separately, not the step divided by three; the Graph's row in the ADR-0003 P3 share ledger; pending S1/S0-f; if missed the number moves (TD), not the design"
  added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: graph_snapshot_restore
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- system: graph_snapshot_restore
  status: proposed
  budget_ms: 0.5
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0012-graph-propagation-scheme.md
  notes: "snapshot(ctx) payload build at most 0.5 ms and at most 32 KB for the MVP ship (about 30.5 KB plus 40 bytes with the hook products); restore plus post_restore at most 2 ms; kernel integration world 3 ms/10 ms is the kernel's; pending S3"
  added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: graph_iterate_to_convergence_or_catch_up
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: graph_iterate_to_convergence_or_catch_up
  status: proposed
  description: "No Graph phase iterates to a convergence condition, recurses, repeats a step or runs a missed step; one pass per loop per step"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0012-graph-propagation-scheme.md
  added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: graph_wall_clock_or_epoch_in_propagation
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: graph_wall_clock_or_epoch_in_propagation
  status: proposed
  description: "No wall clock, restore_epoch, draw_epoch, float or bare % in src/sim/graph/; budgets are counted work units per commit and wall clock on hardware nightly"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0012-graph-propagation-scheme.md
  added: 2026-10-29

registry_candidates.name: graph_hook_product_cache_not_persisted
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: graph_hook_product_cache_not_persisted
  status: proposed
  description: "A value read by a later Graph hook or another block between hooks must be persisted, recomputed at its single point of use from persisted state, or listed as a re-derived cache with a stated window (ADR-0012 section 11); the intensive atmosphere caches are closed out by phase 0 so they hold at every tick boundary"
  adr: docs/architecture/adr-0012-graph-propagation-scheme.md
  added: 2026-10-29

decisions.chosen: Option (a): phase 0 ends by recomputing P, p_o2, o2_pm and trend for every compartment it touched; caches stay DERIVED and exact at every tick boundary

decisions.chosen: (step_no << 26) | (kind << 24) | id, id sized to GraphLimits.ID_MAX = 2^24, key below 2^56
decisions.reason: Ids can exceed any slot count under VS-A churn, so an MVP-only 18-bit field would silently re-introduce node/edge key overlap; golden values computed by arithmetic, not re-probed.

decisions.chosen: (cid << 32) | (crew << 16) | arrival_index and (subject_ref << 32) | (kind << 16) | arrival_index; boot asserts queue bounds <= 65,535
decisions.reason: Widening is cheap and removes the carry into the crew field above 255 entries; D.13 bound below 2^56.
